mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous t-0w collapse of WORKPLACES to -44.3 and jump of RESIDENTIAL to 14.3 identifies a holiday/school-closure week that mechanically depresses the trailing 28-day RETAIL_REC mean. Once that week rolls out of the trailing window and out of the forward window, RETAIL_REC reverts to its pre-holiday level, so the forward 28-day mean exceeds the trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 28.0 points to -44.3 while RESIDENTIAL rose 4.9 points to 14.3 at t-0w
regime_hint: holiday week embedded in steady state
failure_condition: The forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than the trailing 28-day mean of -27.875, i.e. retail does not revert after the holiday week leaves the window.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM rises from 19.7 to 31.0 over three weeks, a precautionary stockpiling signal. Households that front-load grocery and pharmacy baskets cut discretionary trip frequency, so RETAIL_REC declines over the following two weeks before the stockpile is consumed.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 28 percent-change for two consecutive weekly readings
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 19.7 at t-3w to 31.0 at t-1w and held 30.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the two weeks following a GROCERY_PHARM reading above 28 percent-change in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT falls 5.4 points week-on-week to -26.0 at t-0w while PARKS simultaneously improves 6.8 points to -19.6. This divergence shows trips being re-routed to open-air destinations only; because parks trips substitute for mixed indoor trips that carry retail stops, RETAIL_REC is dragged down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops more than 4 points week-on-week while PARKS rises more than 4 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -20.6 at t-1w to -26.0 at t-0w while PARKS rose from -26.4 to -19.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the two weeks after a TRANSIT-down/PARKS-up divergence is equal to or above its prior two-week level in more than half of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Conditional on the holiday-closure configuration (WORKPLACES at or below -40 and RESIDENTIAL at or above 13), retail spending concentrates into a short compressed shopping window rather than spreading across the week. RETAIL_REC therefore rebounds within one week of the closure reading before settling.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES prints at or below -40 percent-change with RESIDENTIAL at or above 13 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC was -25.0 at t-1w and -28.9 at t-0w while WORKPLACES was -16.3 then -44.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the single week after a WORKPLACES print at or below -40 remains at or below the -28.9 t-0w reading.

mechanism_narrative: Excluding the t-0w shock, RETAIL_REC improved monotonically from -30.0 to -27.6 to -25.0 over three weeks, an underlying upward trend in retail activity. The t-0w dip to -28.9 is a one-week shock rather than a trend break, so the forward 28-day mean recovers above the trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -30.0 at t-3w to -25.0 at t-1w, then dipped to -28.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: The forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the trailing mean of -27.875, showing the t-0w dip was a trend break rather than a shock.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL rises 4.9 points week-on-week to 14.3, the highest reading in the four-week window, indicating a durable shift toward staying at home rather than a one-day holiday effect. Persistent at-home behavior removes non-essential retail trips for the full four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 11.0 at t-3w to 14.3 at t-0w, its highest value in the window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the 28 days after a RESIDENTIAL reading above 13 is higher than the preceding 28-day value in more than half of instances.

mechanism_narrative: The pairing of an elevated GROCERY_PHARM (30.0) with a falling TRANSIT (-26.0, down 5.4 points) is an essential-trips-only mobility pattern. When grocery traffic stays high while transit demand drops, discretionary retail footfall is the trip type being cut, so RETAIL_REC remains depressed across four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 25 while TRANSIT falls more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w GROCERY_PHARM was 30.0 and TRANSIT was -26.0, down from -20.6 at t-1w
regime_hint: essential-trips-only regime with rising grocery share
failure_condition: The forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the trailing mean of -27.875 whenever GROCERY_PHARM is above 25 and TRANSIT falls more than 4 points in a week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS improves 6.8 points week-on-week to -19.6, the least-suppressed outdoor reading in the window, indicating loosening constraints on discretionary movement. Rising outdoor trip-making generalizes to other discretionary destinations, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -26.4 at t-1w to -19.6 at t-0w, a 6.8-point improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the two weeks after a PARKS improvement greater than 5 points is at or below its level in the two preceding weeks.
